inherited_methods.consequence: no scalar A+B inequality can close a B-only demand without an explicit conversion map

required_new_information: A precommitted injection or bounded-multiplicity map from distinct owned A atoms, with their endpoint rectangles, to new actual B-reserve atoms.
An owned atomization of S_m with explicit carriers and colour/circuit owner neighbourhoods, including a proof that atoms are not reused across overlapping stars.
A direct outer-A theorem proving R_A<=S_m from rho_A or the union of owned rectangles after cross-star overlap is quotiented.
A joint representation tying every tight B circuit to the same A_<q*, I_mix, N_int, and S_m witness used by the outer gate.
An overlap ledger recording both equality of A diagonals and equality/overlap of canonical B reserves before any scalar aggregation.
A closure calculation showing how the converted units imply D_A=R_A+D_B<=S_m+M_B and then the frozen n^2/8 target in every surviving hard branch.
forbidden_shortcut: No scalar addition, averaging, or min/max of A, B, and S_m quantities counts as a conversion unless every charged unit has a typed carrier and an injective or explicitly bounded-multiplicity ownership map.
